author: J. N. Andrews
text: The ministration in the earthly sanctuary could not actually take away sins; for it had only the blood of bulls and goats to offer. … It is a shadow or representation of the service of Christ in the sanctuary of God in Heaven. Hebrews 8:5; 10:1; Colossians 2:17. … But the ministration of Christ which casts this shadow fills out each part of the work once for all, and is not repeated.
note: The earthly sanctuary service was a shadow of Christ's service in the heavenly sanctuary, which fills out each part once for all (antitype, 1889 Principle X).

author: O. R. L. Crosier
work: The Law of Moses (Day-Star Extra, Cincinnati, February 7, 1846)
text: The atonement which the priest made for the people in connection with their daily ministration was different from that made on the tenth day of the seventh month. In making the former, they went no further than in the Holy; but to make the latter they entered the Holy of Holies — the former was made for individual cases, the latter for the whole nation of Israel collectively — the former was made for the forgiveness of sins, the latter for blotting them out — the former could be made at any time, the latter only on the tenth day of the seventh month.
note: Two apartments, two atonements: the daily one in the Holy for forgiveness; the yearly one (tenth day, seventh month) in the Holy of Holies for blotting sins out.

author: Uriah Smith
text: The antitypical atonement, which is the real removal of sin, was not made when the offering for this dispensation was provided, not by the service of the priest in the first apartment of the sanctuary; but is accomplished only by the service of the priest in the most holy place, which is the closing work of our Lord’s ministration, the cleansing of the sanctuary, a branch of the work which did not commence, as we have seen, till 1844.
note: The atonement proper was made neither at the cross (the offering) nor in the first apartment, but in the most holy place, a work begun in 1844.

author: J. H. Waggoner
text: It does not seem to admit of a doubt that the judgment of the saints, the blotting out of sin, the making of the atonement, and the cleansing of the sanctuary, are identical. And we have seen that in the type the atonement was made—the sanctuary cleansed, when the high priest went into the most holy place before the ark; and the most holy was opened only on the day of atonement. … Under the sounding of the seventh trumpet it is said, “The temple of God was opened in Heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament.” Revelation 11:19.
note: Judgment of the saints = blotting out = atonement = cleansing; the high priest before the ark answers to Rev 11:19, which the next paragraph (AERS 221.1) dates to 1844.

author: Ellen G. White
text: And as the typical cleansing of the earthly was accomplished by the removal of the sins by which it had been polluted, so the actual cleansing of the heavenly is to be accomplished by the removal, or blotting out, of the sins which are there recorded. But before this can be accomplished, there must be an examination of the books of record to determine who, through repentance of sin and faith in Christ, are entitled to the benefits of His atonement. The cleansing of the sanctuary therefore involves a work of investigation—a work of judgment. This work must be performed prior to the coming of Christ to redeem His people; for when He comes, His reward is with Him to give to every man according to his works. Revelation 22:12.
note: The cleansing is the blotting out of recorded sins, preceded by an examination of the books of record: an investigative judgment before the advent.

author: Ellen G. White
text: It was seen, also, that while the sin offering pointed to Christ as a sacrifice, and the high priest represented Christ as a mediator, the scapegoat typified Satan, the author of sin, upon whom the sins of the truly penitent will finally be placed. When the high priest, by virtue of the blood of the sin offering, removed the sins from the sanctuary, he placed them upon the scapegoat. When Christ, by virtue of His own blood, removes the sins of His people from the heavenly sanctuary at the close of His ministration, He will place them upon Satan, who, in the execution of the judgment, must bear the final penalty.
note: Sin offering = Christ the sacrifice; high priest = Christ the mediator; scapegoat = Satan, who receives the sins only after the sanctuary is cleansed.
